Review Comment: I'm not sure this is a good idea because there are times when `rollback` should be called instead. For example: ```java try (TransactionCatalog txnCat = ...) { data = readData(txnCat, srcTable); writeData(txnCat, destTable, data); deleteData(txnCat, srcTable, data); } ``` If `writeData` succeeds, then `deleteData` fails (maybe it's interrupted) before it creates the delete operation, then closing would complete the write without knowing that the delete didn't finish and should be rolled back. I think the fix is to accept a flag, although I'm not sure we'd want to do this: ```java TransactionCatalog txnCat = ... boolean rollback = true; try { data = readData(txnCat, srcTable); writeData(txnCat, destTable, data); deleteData(txnCat, srcTable, data); rollback = false; } finally { txnCat.close(rollback); } ``` Passing a flag means you can no longer use try-with-resources, so I don't see much point to a `close(boolean)` method.
